chunks: From him, from al-Nadr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who comes to a barren land, reclaims it, channels its rivers, develops it, and cultivates it. What is incumbent upon him? He said: 'He must pay the khums.' I said: 'If he knows the owner, what then?' He said: 'He should return his right to him.'

key_terms.الْأَرْضَ الْخَرِبَةَ: Barren land (land not claimed or cultivated)
key_terms.الْخُمُسُ: Khums (one-fifth tax, implied by الصَّدَقَةُ in this context of land reclamation)

ai.seo_question: What are the financial obligations of khums and owner's rights when reclaiming barren land in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of land reclamation (iqra'), distinguishing between the general obligation of zakat on agricultural produce and the specific rights of previous owners. While the summary mentions khums, the text explicitly states 'al-sadaqah' (zakat), reflecting the Shia view that land reclamation incurs zakat on the yield, with compensation to the original owner only if their ownership rights are recognized and not extinguished by abandonment.
